title: Comment adverbs and viewpoint adverbs
subtitle: Presumably, ... / Financially, ...
summary: Comment on what you say with adverbs like presumably and rightly, and say what angle you are speaking from with viewpoint adverbs and phrases.

lesson.heading: Three things a comment adverb can do
rows: how likely we think something is
apparently, certainly, clearly, definitely, obviously, presumably, probably, undoubtedly
our attitude to, or opinion of, what is said
astonishingly, frankly, generally, honestly, interestingly, luckily, naturally, sadly, seriously, surprisingly, unbelievably
bravely, carelessly, foolishly, generously, kindly, rightly, stupidly, wisely, wrongly

lesson.heading: Position and punctuation
lesson.text: Comment adverbs often apply to the whole sentence and are most frequently used in front position, although they can also come at the end or in other positions. At the beginning and end of a sentence we usually separate them from the rest by a comma in writing, or by intonation in speech.

examples.text: **Presumably**, he didn't hear me when I called.
The book was based on his experience in China, **apparently**.
If you practise continuously, you will **undoubtedly** get better.

lesson.heading: Adverbs of judgement follow the subject
lesson.text: Comment adverbs which show a judgement of someone's actions usually come straight after the subject, though they can be moved to front position for emphasis.

examples.text: He **kindly** offered to give me a lift.
examples.note: or Kindly, he offered ... to emphasise 'Kindly'

examples.text: The builders **generously** agreed to plant new trees to replace the ones they had dug up.
Most people **rightly** believe that the prisoners should be released.

lesson.heading: The whole sentence, or just one word?

left.label: Comment on the whole sentence - front position
examples: **Astonishingly**, she did well in the exam.
= I was surprised that she did well
You've had a major operation. **Obviously**, it will be very painful for a while.
= I expect you to know this already

right.label: Modifying one word - other positions
examples: She did **astonishingly** well in the exam.
When he stood up it was **obviously** very painful.
= the pain was clear to see

lesson.heading: Viewpoint adverbs
lesson.text: Viewpoint adverbs make clear what viewpoint we are speaking from - that is, which features of something we are talking about.

examples.text: **Financially**, the accident has been a disaster for the owners of the tunnel.
The brothers may be alike **physically**, but they have very different personalities.
The country earns most of its income from agriculture and **industrially** it is relatively undeveloped.

lesson.note: Also: biologically, environmentally, ideologically, logically, medically, morally, outwardly, politically, technically, visually.

lesson.heading: Viewpoint phrases
lesson.text: A number of phrases do the same job as a viewpoint adverb, and are often more natural in longer, more formal sentences.

examples.text: **Politically** / **In political terms**, this summer is a crucial time for the government.
**From a grammatical point of view** the essay was well written, but its style was inappropriate.
The result is a severe blow to the country **as far as democracy is concerned**.

lesson.note: Also: politically speaking, in terms of politics.

lesson.heading: Whose viewpoint is it?
lesson.text: Some adverbs and phrases say whose viewpoint we are expressing.

examples.text: The head of National Bank is to receive, **according to reports**, a £1 million bonus.
**In my view**, the foreign minister should resign immediately.

lesson.note: Also: to my / his / her knowledge, from my / his / her perspective, personally, in my / his / her opinion.

lesson.text: Same adverb, two jobs: at the front with a comma it comments on the whole sentence; next to an adjective or adverb it simply strengthens that word.

exercises.prompt: ___, no paintings were destroyed by the fire in the gallery.
exercises.explanation: A comment adverb in front position: it was very surprising indeed that nothing was destroyed.

exercises.prompt: As you drive off the ferry, there are lots of different flags flying by the side of the road. ___, the idea is to welcome visitors from other countries.
exercises.explanation: Presumably shows how likely the speaker thinks the explanation is.

exercises.prompt: Most people ___ believe that the prisoners should be released.
exercises.explanation: Rightly judges the action, so it comes straight after the subject.

exercises.prompt: He ___ broke the window when he was painting, because he wasn't paying attention to what he was doing.
exercises.explanation: Another adverb of judgement, again just after the subject.

exercises.statement: The book was based on his experience in China, apparently.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Comment adverbs can also come at the end, separated by a comma.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'she did extremely well in the exam'?
options: She did astonishingly well in the exam.
Astonishingly, she did well in the exam.
She astonishingly did well in the exam.
exercises.explanation: Next to the adverb well, astonishingly strengthens it; in front position it would comment on the whole sentence (= I was surprised).

exercises.prompt: Match each opening to the ending that its viewpoint adverb prepares us for.

pairs.left: Thomas says that he is still getting severe headaches, although medically
pairs.right: the doctors can't find anything wrong.

pairs.left: As she stepped onto the stage she felt terrified, but outwardly
Now that lead is no longer added to most petrol, environmentally
pairs.right: it is no longer the problem it once was.

pairs.left: The band didn't play terribly well, and the singing was awful, but visually
Hansen is one of the richest men in the country, although politically
pairs.right: he claims to be a socialist.

pairs.left: The cost of living is much lower in the north, so financially
pairs.right: we'd be much better off if we moved there.

exercises.prompt: Julie is likely to be fined for failing to pay her gas bill, although ___ she could be sent to prison.
exercises.explanation: The viewpoint is that of the letter of the law, so technically.

exercises.prompt: What does each comment adverb show?
In ___ terms, limestone is a relatively new rock.
exercises.explanation: In + adjective + terms is one of the standard viewpoint phrases.

exercises.prompt: ___ speaking, in what ways has disease affected the development of Western civilisation?
exercises.explanation: Adverb + speaking is another way of naming the viewpoint.

exercises.answer: From a grammatical point of view the essay was well written, but its style was inappropriate.
exercises.explanation: From a ... point of view names the angle we are judging from.
